options.text: Reverend, I couldn't help noticing your bell.
options.say: A half-step flat since the day it was hung, and I have struck it every morning for six years, and I will tell you a secret, Mr. Grubb: I have stopped hearing it.
options.echo: Reverend, I couldn't help noticing your bell. Tell me about it.

options.say: Feeling is free. Articulated feeling is priced by the adjective. The board is by the door.

options.text: Do you believe in Mott's gold?
options.say: I believe in what fills my pews, and Mr. Mott fills them better than I do. I try not to examine the arrangement.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: A man of— a man of real—

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: I never met him. The undertaker knew him best. Professionally.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: I grieve for Mr. Pike every Sunday, Mr. Grubb, out of habit.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: Nobody has ever paid me to.

options.text: You have a fine speaking voice.
I'd like to arrange a funeral.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: Pike! Six years in the ground and never sung over. The undertaker did him on credit and nobody came.

options.text: Mr. Sheng says you owe him for linens.
options.say: I do, and I shall pay him on the next occasion of grief. I carry no money on ordinary days, Mr. Grubb. It would only come between me and the poor.

repeats.say: On the next occasion of grief, Mr. Grubb. I pray for one daily, in general terms.

options.text: Could Mr. Pike have another service?
options.say: An anniversary! Grief keeps whatever calendar it likes. Have Frame print it.

options.text: Have you ever won an Assay, Reverend?

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: Once, God forgive me. A mourner told me at the graveside, 'My father died rich,' and I said, 'Your father died owing me two dollars, and I have chosen to regard it as a legacy.'

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: The whole hill applauded. It was a very successful funeral.

options.text: Thank you. This has been clarifying.

SOW_C1.prompt: And how shall we remember the departed?

opening.speaker: sowerby
opening.line: And how shall we remember the departed?

options.text: He was a beloved and industrious young man of rare promise.
options.say: Beloved! Industrious! Young! Rare! Four adjectives, eight dollars, and every one of them deserved.
That is not a eulogy, that is a census.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: A long pause. He writes it down.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: …Present. Three words, and one of them is 'was'. I shall add an 'amen' at no charge; I cannot send a man into the ground on three.

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: He tuned pianos. He brought order to the very instruments of praise, and asked nothing, and was paid less—

exchange.speaker: sowerby
exchange.line: He goes on. He is still going when Thad looks back from the door.
